"""Remember: file one Tier A memory in plain code, no model call.

The writer (Eric, or an agent following the memory-write skill) supplies the words;
this does the filing the skill asks for: name rule, duplicate check, frontmatter,
the MEMORY.md index line, read-back check, and a recall.py index refresh.
Tier A only. Tier B (global-memory MEMORY.md / USER.md) has caps that need judgement.

Usage:
    python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type project --name cloud-push-launchd-blocked \\
        --desc "one line: what the fact is" --hook "when to open it" \\
        --why "reason" --how "what to do" "The fact itself."
    echo "body" | python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py ... -      # body from stdin
    ... --update      # replace an existing memory of the same name
    ... --force       # file it although a similar name exists
    ... --dir PATH    # memory folder (default: the slug of the current folder)

Exit 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL (bad input or read-back failed), 2 = refused (it exists or looks like a duplicate).
"""
import argparse
import importlib.util
import os
import re
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("recall", os.path.join(HERE, "recall.py"))
recall = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(recall)

TYPES = ("user", "feedback", "project", "reference")
NAME = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
INDEX_LIMIT = 200  # the harness stops reading a memory index after about this many lines


def slug_dir(cwd):
    """The skill's slug rule: every character other than a letter or digit becomes '-'."""
    return os.path.join(recall.HOME, ".claude/projects", re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "-", cwd), "memory")


def name_words(stem):
    return set(re.split(r"[-_]", stem)) - set(TYPES) - {""}


def look_alikes(mem_dir, name):
    """Existing memories whose name shares at least half its words with the new name."""
    new = name_words(name)
    out = []
    for f in sorted(os.listdir(mem_dir)) if os.path.isdir(mem_dir) else []:
        if f.endswith(".md") and f != "MEMORY.md":
            old = name_words(f[:-3].split("_", 1)[-1])
            if new and old and len(new & old) * 2 >= max(len(new), len(old)):
                out.append(f)
    return out


def render(a, body):
    desc = a.desc.replace('"', "'")
    text = f'---\nname: {a.name}\ndescription: "{desc}"\nmetadata:\n  type: {a.type}\n---\n\n{body.strip()}\n'
    if a.why:
        text += f"\n**Why:** {a.why.strip()}\n"
    if a.how:
        text += f"\n**How to apply:** {a.how.strip()}\n"
    return text


def write_atomic(path, text):
    tmp = path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(text)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def set_index_line(index, fname, line):
    """Add the pointer, or replace the one already pointing at fname. Returns the new index text."""
    text = open(index, encoding="utf-8").read() if os.path.exists(index) else "# Memory Index\n"
    lines = text.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if f"]({fname})" in l]
    if hits:
        lines[hits[0]] = line
        lines = [l for i, l in enumerate(lines) if i not in hits[1:]]
    else:
        lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def verify(path, index, a, body):
    """The skill's verification gate, in code. Returns a list of failed checks."""
    fails = []
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    m = re.match(r"---\n(.*?)\n---\n", text, re.S)
    if not m:
        fails.append("frontmatter missing")
    else:
        fm = m.group(1)
        for want in (f"name: {a.name}", "description: ", f"  type: {a.type}"):
            if want not in fm:
                fails.append(f"frontmatter lacks '{want.strip()}'")
    if text.count(body.strip()) != 1:
        fails.append("fact not in the file exactly once")
    fname = os.path.basename(path)
    n = open(index, encoding="utf-8").read().count(f"]({fname})")
    if n != 1:
        fails.append(f"index points at {fname} {n} times, want 1")
    return fails


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("body", help="the fact; '-' reads it from stdin")
    ap.add_argument("--type", required=True, choices=TYPES)
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="bare kebab slug, e.g. cloud-push-launchd-blocked")
    ap.add_argument("--desc", required=True, help="one line; used to decide relevance during recall")
    ap.add_argument("--hook", required=True, help="index hook: when to open this memory")
    ap.add_argument("--title", help="index title (default: from the name)")
    ap.add_argument("--why")
    ap.add_argument("--how")
    ap.add_argument("--dir", help="memory folder (default: slug of the current folder)")
    ap.add_argument("--update", action="store_true", help="replace an existing memory of this name")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="file it although a similar name exists")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    body = sys.stdin.read() if a.body == "-" else a.body
    errs = []
    if not body.strip():
        errs.append("the fact is empty")
    if not NAME.match(a.name):
        errs.append(f"--name '{a.name}' is not a bare kebab slug (a-z, 0-9, single dashes)")
    elif a.name.split("-")[0] == a.type:
        errs.append(f"--name repeats the type: use '{a.name.split('-', 1)[-1]}' (only if the memory is not about '{a.type}')")
    for flag in ("desc", "hook", "title"):
        if "\n" in (getattr(a, flag) or ""):
            errs.append(f"--{flag} must be one line")
    if errs:
        print("FAIL: " + "; ".join(errs))
        return 1

    mem_dir = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(a.dir)) if a.dir else slug_dir(os.getcwd())
    fname = f"{a.type}_{a.name}.md"
    path = os.path.join(mem_dir, fname)
    index = os.path.join(mem_dir, "MEMORY.md")

    if os.path.exists(path) and not a.update:
        print(f"REFUSED: {path} exists. Read it; to replace it, add --update.")
        return 2
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        twins = [f for f in look_alikes(mem_dir, a.name) if f != fname]
        if twins and not a.force:
            print(f"REFUSED: similar memory names in {mem_dir}: {', '.join(twins)}")
            print("Read them first. Update one (--name <its name> --update), or add --force if this is a new fact.")
            return 2

    os.makedirs(mem_dir, exist_ok=True)
    title = a.title or a.name.replace("-", " ").capitalize()
    write_atomic(path, render(a, body))
    write_atomic(index, set_index_line(index, fname, f"- [{title}]({fname}) — {a.hook.strip()}"))

    fails = verify(path, index, a, body)
    if fails:
        print(f"FAIL: {path}: " + "; ".join(fails))
        return 1

    notes = []
    if not os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(mem_dir)).startswith("-Users-") and not a.dir:
        notes.append("this is not a Mac slug; it will not be auto-injected on this machine")
    lines = open(index, encoding="utf-8").read().count("\n")
    if lines > INDEX_LIMIT:
        notes.append(f"index is {lines} lines; the harness reads about {INDEX_LIMIT}")
    rts = recall.roots()
    if any(os.path.abspath(mem_dir).startswith(os.path.abspath(r)) for r in rts):
        recall.open_index(rts).close()  # findable by recall.py right away
    else:
        notes.append("folder is outside the recall/memsearch roots (KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json); search will not find it")

    print(f"PASS: {'updated' if a.update else 'saved'} {path.replace(recall.HOME, '~')}")
    for n in notes:
        print(f"note: {n}")
    print("Active from the next session.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Checks remember.py on a temp memory folder: save, refuse, update, look-alike guard, bad input.
Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_remember.py  (writes only inside a temp folder)
"""
import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import os
import tempfile

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "remember", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "remember.py"))
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)


def run(*args):
    out = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
        code = m.main(list(args))
    return code, out.getvalue()


# Slug rule from the skill.
assert m.slug_dir("/Users/kristinarash/DEV").endswith("/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory")

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    base = ["--dir", d, "--type", "project", "--desc", 'Drive "push" fix', "--hook", "cloud-push fails"]

    # Save: file with frontmatter, Why/How, one index line.
    code, out = run(*base, "--name", "push-fix", "--why", "launchd lacks access", "--how", "run in Terminal",
                    "Run cloud-push from Terminal.")
    assert code == 0 and "PASS" in out, out
    text = open(os.path.join(d, "project_push-fix.md")).read()
    assert text.startswith("---\nname: push-fix\ndescription: \"Drive 'push' fix\"\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n")
    assert "**Why:** launchd lacks access" in text and "**How to apply:** run in Terminal" in text
    idx = open(os.path.join(d, "MEMORY.md")).read()
    assert idx.count("](project_push-fix.md)") == 1 and "- [Push fix](project_push-fix.md) — cloud-push fails" in idx

    # Same name again: refused, file untouched.
    code, out = run(*base, "--name", "push-fix", "Something else.")
    assert code == 2 and "REFUSED" in out and "Terminal" in open(os.path.join(d, "project_push-fix.md")).read()

    # Update: body replaced, still one index line.
    code, out = run(*base, "--name", "push-fix", "--update", "--hook", "push to Drive fails", "Run it via cloud-push-launch.sh.")
    assert code == 0, out
    assert "cloud-push-launch.sh" in open(os.path.join(d, "project_push-fix.md")).read()
    idx = open(os.path.join(d, "MEMORY.md")).read()
    assert idx.count("](project_push-fix.md)") == 1 and "push to Drive fails" in idx

    # Look-alike name: refused unless --force.
    code, out = run(*base, "--name", "push-fix-drive", "A near twin.")
    assert code == 2 and "project_push-fix.md" in out, out
    code, out = run(*base, "--name", "push-fix-drive", "--force", "A near twin.")
    assert code == 0, out

    # Bad input: not a slug, type repeated in the name, two-line hook, empty fact.
    assert run(*base, "--name", "Push_Fix", "x")[0] == 1
    assert run(*base, "--name", "project-thing", "x")[0] == 1
    assert run("--dir", d, "--type", "user", "--name", "a-b", "--desc", "d", "--hook", "a\nb", "x")[0] == 1
    assert run(*base, "--name", "empty-one", "   ")[0] == 1

---
name: memory-write
description: >-
  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
  recall checks the injected snapshot, then recall.py, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
---

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.

   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the words in the question are not the words in the notes: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- **Deliverables.** A finished file made for someone else this session (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a copy at `~/DEV/_DRIVE/03_REPORTS/YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>`. The repo keeps the source; Drive keeps the handed-off copy. Name the copy in the report.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If not empty, surface it and fix the hook issue if obvious, then append its lines to `transcripts/.errors.log.archived-<YYYY-MM-DD>` and clear it with `cp /dev/null` (same archive-then-clear step as backup and claude-stack-doctor; `: > file` is dcg-blocked).
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- **Deliverables.** A finished file made for someone else this session (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a copy at `~/DEV/_DRIVE/03_REPORTS/YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>`. The repo keeps the source; Drive keeps the handed-off copy. Name the copy in the report.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If not empty, surface it and fix the hook issue if obvious, then append its lines to `transcripts/.errors.log.archived-<YYYY-MM-DD>` and clear it with `cp /dev/null` (same archive-then-clear step as backup and claude-stack-doctor; `: > file` is dcg-blocked).
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# 2026-10-23 — recall.py and remember.py (second-brain principles 3 and 5)

## Why
Eric reviewed "Second Brain - Principles and Starter Prompts" (RoboNuggets, `~/Desktop/EricWork/`).
The setup had 3 of 5 principles. Missing: #3 deterministic code before the model (a retrieval
ladder and a no-model write), and #5 make it prove itself against a fresh default session.

## What was built
- `~/.claude/scripts/recall.py` — plain-code recall, ~1 s. SQLite FTS5 BM25 over the memsearch
  roots + the whole SecondBrain vault + every `~/.claude/projects/*/memory` folder (31 folders,
  336 files). A Tier A memory in the top 3 moves to #1 when its file name matches as many question
  words as #1's name; the newest Mac/Windows copy of a memory wins and is listed once. Opens only
  the best file; prints matching paragraphs with line numbers (short files whole); one gated
  pointer hop. Index: `~/.claude/cache/recall-fts.sqlite`, mtime-refreshed under a write lock.
  Tests: `python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_recall.py`.
- `~/.claude/scripts/remember.py` — files one Tier A memory with no model: name rule, refuses an
  existing or look-alike name (exit 2; `--update` / `--force`), frontmatter, MEMORY.md index line,
  read-back check, recall index refresh. Mac slugs keep `_`. Tier B stays manual (caps).
  Tests: `python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_remember.py`.
- Bench `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/` (questions.tsv, run.sh, score.py, results.md). 9
  questions; Q6-9 written before any code. `out*/` gitignored (evidence can hold athlete names).
- `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/recall-eval.py` — now uses recall.py's BM25 (one home) and has a
  `recall` backend that ranks as recall.py does.

## Results
| | default session | memsearch | recall.py (run 4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Correct | 6/9 | 1.5/5 | 8/9 |
| Tokens / question | ~100k | ~18k | ~18k |
| Search time | n/a | 53-166 s | ~1 s |

30-case eval hit@1: fts5 19, recall.py 21 (22 before the extra memory folders; p02 moved 1 -> 2
behind a same-day handoff). A fresh headless session in `~/DEV` used recall.py unprompted.

## Decisions (and why)
- Kept fts5 BM25 for ranking: my index-only ranker lost to it on the 30-case eval (17 vs 19 hit@1).
- Tier A first, name-guarded: compiled articles gave a stale fix (Full Disk Access) over the newer
  memory. A body-coverage guard let an off-topic memory jump (n03); the file-name guard does not.
- Newest copy wins between Mac and Windows slugs: the Windows copy is sometimes newer.
- Routing switched (Eric: "switch now", "switch both"): `~/DEV/CLAUDE.md`, memory-write skill,
  `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, memory-compiler `hooks/session-start.py`. memsearch is the NO MATCH fallback.
- The 10-23 `.errors.log` bursts were this bench (`claude -p --no-session-persistence` from `~/DEV`).

## Files changed
`~/.claude/scripts/{recall.py,test_recall.py,remember.py,test_remember.py}`,
`~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/*`, `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/{recall-eval.py,ledger.md,results/2026-10-23-*}`,
`~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, `~/.claude/.gitignore`, `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md`,
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/hooks/session-start.py`, `~/DEV/CLAUDE.md`, `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md`,
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/{reference_recall-bench.md,MEMORY.md}`.

## Next
1. Optional: add `SecondBrain/Notes/`, `Drafts/`, `Inbox/`, `audits/` to
   `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` so memsearch (the fallback) sees them. Needs a
   memsearch rebuild; `memsearch index` is destructive — read Tier A `memsearch-index-is-destructive` first.
2. Bench miss Q3: `project_drive-fuse-read-hang.md` does not reach the top 3. Do not tune on one question.
3. Optional: run the bench with the monthly `/brain-audit` (~$0.60 a run).

## Gotchas
- Each headless bench run adds harmless `transcript_path does not exist` lines to `.errors.log`.
- Vague questions can still rank vault notes or knowledge articles above a project's own memory.

content.content:
Exit code 1

`memsearch index <paths>` is **never read-only**. It reconciles the collection against
the path set it is given and deletes every indexed source not under those paths
(core.py `index()` → store.py delete). An empty or partial path set wipes the rest.

On 2026-10-07 a diagnostic run against an empty temp dir deleted ~12,900 of ~31,000
vectors before it was stopped. Recovery: a full re-index over all 13 paths in
`KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json`, which takes hours on Windows (~3 s/chunk).
`memsearch stats` counts tombstones until compaction, so use `count(*)` for live rows.

**Why:** a "just timing it" run silently destroyed 40% of the index.
**How to apply:** never pass a test or partial path set to `memsearch index`. To time
indexing, use a throwaway collection or time `memsearch search`. For a catch-up run,
use `~/.claude/scripts/memsearch-drain.ps1`: it resolves the full path set and holds
the hook's lock.

Windows failure causes found the same day:
- **10-06 "Milvus unreachable":** Docker Desktop's vpnkit port forward to
  milvus-standalone flapped after days of uptime through Modern Standby. Milvus itself
  never restarted. A Docker restart cleared it.
- **10-07 ETIMEDOUT ×9:** low free RAM (1–2 GB) slowed indexing to ~1.2 s/chunk, so the
  hook's 600s cap killed every run partway. The cap was raised to 3h on 2026-10-07.
  The streak never resets on Windows because no nightly reindex runs there.

Related: [[memsearch-hook-timeout-cap]], [[automation-cadence]].

content.content:
`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` is the single source of truth for which directories memsearch indexes. Three writers read it: the SessionEnd hook `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (nightly; 09:00 since 2026-08-29), and the Codex hook `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1`.

**Found 2026-08-14:** the JS hook pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` — the pre-migration Windows layout. DEV lives at `~/DEV` on this Mac, so the read threw, the `catch` returned a hardcoded fallback, and the hook indexed **4 paths instead of 10** for months. The fallback itself was also stale (`~/Desktop/SecondBrain/...`, which does not exist since the vault move). `daily-backup.ps1` used `$U/DEV` and was already correct; the Codex hook self-locates from its own script path and was fine. So only the JS hook drifted — and it is the one wired into `settings.json` (`SessionEnd`, 50s timeout).

Unindexed as a result: `SecondBrain/Knowledge`, `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`, `SecondBrain/morning-briefings`, the Mac memory slug `-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory`, `KeystoneOS/decisions`, `.codex/memories`. Incremental recall for all of those depended entirely on that nightly.

**Why:** the failure mode was invisible. A silent `catch → fallback` means a migration-broken config path degrades into a quieter, smaller, still-succeeding job — no error, no log line, no failed run. Nothing surfaces until someone asks "why didn't that turn up in search?" The bug was not the wrong path; it was that the wrong path cost nothing to have.

**How to apply:**
- Any config-file fallback in this stack must log to `.errors.log` when it fires. The JS hook now does. A fallback that never announces itself is a silent outage with a long tail.
- When auditing post-migration breakage, grep for `Desktop/DEV` and `Desktop/SecondBrain` — those two strings mark Windows-era assumptions. Do not trust that a script "works" as evidence its paths resolved; check what it actually resolved to.
- Verify path config by resolving it in isolation (`node -e` reading the same JSON, printing EXISTS/MISSING per entry) rather than by running the indexer — that proves the fix without taking the Milvus Lite write lock.
- Paths in the JSON that do not exist yet are harmless; every writer filters through an existence check before passing them to memsearch.

**There were TWO copies of this hook, and fixing one did not fix the other (2026-08-15).** A Codex review found `~/.codex/hooks.json` wires its *own* copy at `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, separate from the Claude copy at `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`. The Claude copy was repaired 2026-08-14; the Codex copy still pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/...`, so **every Codex session-end indexed a stale 5-path fallback** that also referenced the old `~/Desktop/SecondBrain` — missing SecondBrain/Knowledge, Inbox/meetings, morning-briefings, KeystoneOS decisions and the Mac memory slug. Now fixed and verified resolving all 11 configured paths.

Ordering trap in that repair: `const ERR_LOG` was declared *after* `const PATHS = resolvePaths()`. Adding a `logErr()` call inside `resolvePaths` therefore hit the const temporal dead zone, and `logErr`'s own `try/catch` swallowed the ReferenceError — reproducing the silent fallback the fix was meant to remove. `ERR_LOG` must be declared before `PATHS`.

**How to apply:** when fixing a hook, first ask *which copy the harness actually wires* — check `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, not just the file you happened to open. Grep the whole home tree for the hook's basename before assuming there is one.

**A THIRD hook had the same stale path, found 2026-09-01 during `/doctor-plus`.** `~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js` (SessionStart) read `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/unified-snapshot.md`, threw ENOENT, and its `catch (_) { emit(null) }` injected **nothing at all** — for every session since the migration. The snapshot file was being written correctly the whole time at `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/`; only the reader was wrong. Zero symptoms: no error, no log, valid JSON on stdout, session starts normally.

The 2026-08-14/15 sweep fixed the two `memsearch-sync.js` copies but did not catch this one, so **"grep for `Desktop/DEV`" must cover every file in `~/.claude/hooks/` and `~/.codex/hooks/`, not only the hook currently being repaired.** Run it as a sweep across the whole hooks tree, not per-file.

That sweep then found a **fourth** copy — `~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`, byte-identical and wired in `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Also fixed 2026-09-01.

**A second signature the `Desktop/DEV` grep cannot catch:** `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (dated 2026-08-08) had been through a bad `claude` to `Codex` find-replace, so it told Codex to read `~/.Codex/global-memory/`, `~/.Codex/projects/<slug>/memory/` and `~/.Codex/Codex-memory-compiler/daily/` — none of which exist. 7:# index with no cap, once, then gets out of the way.
8:#
9:# Coordination: holds ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.memsearch-index.lock
10:# with THIS process's PID for the whole run (the hook skips while the owner is
11:# alive), and refreshes .memsearch-last-run so the hook's 30-min cooldown is in
12:# force when it finishes. Runs BelowNormal so interactive work keeps the CPU.
13:# batch_size comes from ~/.memsearch/config.toml (8 since 2026-09-28).
15:$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
16:$T       = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\global-memory\transcripts'
17:$lock    = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-index.lock'
18:$lastRun = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-last-run'
19:$streak  = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-timeout-streak'
20:$log     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
21:$exe     = Join-Path $env:APPDATA 'Python\Python314\Scripts\memsearch.exe'
22:New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Split-Path $log) | Out-Null
23:function Log($m) { Add-Content -LiteralPath $log -Value "[$((Get-Date).ToString('s'))] $m" }
25:# Same path source as memsearch-sync.js.
26:$dev  = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Desktop\DEV'
27:$vault = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Desktop\SecondBrain'   # {VAULT}; this script is Windows-only

29:$paths = @($cfg.paths | ForEach-Object {
30:    ($_ -replace '\{HOME\}', $env:USERPROFILE -replace '\{DEV\}', $dev -replace '\{VAULT\}', $vault) -replace '/', '\'
31:} | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ })
33:# Take the lock atomically; wait up to 20 min for a live hook run to finish.
34:$deadline = (Get-Date).AddMinutes(20)
35:while ($true) {
36:    try {
37:        $fs = [IO.File]::Open($lock, [IO.FileMode]::CreateNew); $fs.Close()
38:        [IO.File]::WriteAllText($lock, [string]$PID); break
39:    } catch {
40:        $owner = 0; try { $owner = [int](Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $lock) } catch {}

42:            if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) { Log "gave up: lock held by live pid $owner"; exit 1 }

44:        }
45:        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $lock -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
46:    }
47:}
49:try {
50:    Set-Content -LiteralPath $lastRun -Value "$((Get-Date).ToString('o')) drain pid=$PID"
51:    (Get-Process -Id $PID).PriorityClass = 'BelowNormal'   # children inherit
52:    $env:PYTHONIOENCODING = 'utf-8'; $env:PYTHONUTF8 = '1'
53:    $out = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'memsearch-drain.out'; $err = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'memsearch-drain.err'
54:    Log "start: $($paths.Count) paths"
55:    $sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
56:    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList (@('index') + $paths) -NoNewWindow -PassThru `
57:         -RedirectStandardOutput $out -RedirectStandardError $err
58:    $null = $p.Handle
59:    $p.WaitForExit()
60:    $tail = ((Get-Content -LiteralPath $out, $err -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) | Select-Object -Last 5) -join ' | '

1:# memsearch-drain.ps1 -- one-off foreground catch-up of the memsearch backlog.
2:#
3:# Why (2026-09-28, Windows laptop): ~10,100 chunks were never indexed. The
4:# SessionEnd hook caps each run at 600s and this CPU embeds ~5 s/chunk with
5:# bge-m3, so every run was killed after ~110 chunks and the next session end
6:# restarted it -- 2.5-3 GB of RAM all day. This runs the same incremental
7:# index with no cap, once, then gets out of the way.
8:#
9:# Coordination: holds ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.memsearch-index.lock
10:# with THIS process's PID for the whole run (the hook skips while the owner is
11:# alive), and refreshes .memsearch-last-run so the hook's 30-min cooldown is in
12:# force when it finishes. Runs BelowNormal so interactive work keeps the CPU.
13:# batch_size comes from ~/.memsearch/config.toml (8 since 2026-09-28).
15:$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
16:$T       = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\global-memory\transcripts'
17:$lock    = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-index.lock'
18:$lastRun = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-last-run'
19:$streak  = Join-Path $T '.memsearch-timeout-streak'
20:$log     = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude\scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
21:$exe     = Join-Path $env:APPDATA 'Python\Python314\Scripts\memsearch.exe'
22:New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Split-Path $log) | Out-Null
23:function Log($m) { Add-Content -LiteralPath $log -Value "[$((Get-Date).ToString('s'))] $m" }
25:# Same path source as memsearch-sync.js.
26:$dev  = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Desktop\DEV'
27:$vault = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Desktop\SecondBrain'   # {VAULT}; this script is Windows-only
28:$cfg  = Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $dev 'KeystoneOS\data\memory-index-paths.json') | ConvertFrom-Json
29:$paths = @($cfg.paths | ForEach-Object {
30:    ($_ -replace '\{HOME\}', $env:USERPROFILE -replace '\{DEV\}', $dev -replace '\{VAULT\}', $vault) -replace '/', '\'
31:} | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ })
33:# Take the lock atomically; wait up to 20 min for a live hook run to finish.
34:$deadline = (Get-Date).AddMinutes(20)
35:while ($true) {

37:        $fs = [IO.File]::Open($lock, [IO.FileMode]::CreateNew); $fs.Close()

42:            if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) { Log "gave up: lock held by live pid $owner"; exit 1 }
43:            Start-Sleep -Seconds 30; continue
44:        }
45:        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $lock -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
46:    }
47:}

import datetime
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import cards

STATUS = """# STATUS

## Done
- 2026-09-14: **Prioritization system shipped.** Design in `docs/x.md`.
  - sub detail
- 2026-10-03: Org step 1 done.
- 2026-10-03: Org step 2 done, `portfolio.json` backfilled.

## Next
- **Build the PM system.** Start at step 1.
- second thing

## Open questions
- 2026-12-01: a dated question that is not progress

## Gotchas
- 2027-01-01: a dated gotcha that is not progress
"""


class TestParseStatus(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_stands_is_the_newest_dated_entry_last_one_wins_a_tie(self):
        got = cards.parse_status(STATUS)
        self.assertEqual(got["stands_date"], "2026-10-03")
        self.assertEqual(got["stands"], "Org step 2 done, portfolio.json backfilled.")

    def test_next_is_the_first_item_with_markdown_stripped(self):
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(STATUS)["next"], "Build the PM system. Start at step 1.")

    def test_current_state_section_counts_as_progress(self):
        text = "## Current state\n- 2026-09-01: older\n- 2026-09-20: newer\n\n## Next\n-\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual((got["stands_date"], got["stands"]), ("2026-09-20", "newer"))

    def test_an_empty_next_is_none(self):
        self.assertIsNone(cards.parse_status("## Next\n-\n\n## Open questions\n- x\n")["next"])

    def test_dated_headings_and_bold_dates_count(self):
        text = "## 2026-10-02 (Mac): heading entry\n\n- **2026-10-01 (Windows): bold entry.** more\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual((got["stands_date"], got["stands"]), ("2026-10-02", "(Mac): heading entry"))

    def test_no_dates_and_no_next(self):
        got = cards.parse_status("# STATUS\n\nfree text\n")
        self.assertEqual(got, {"stands": None, "stands_date": None, "next": None})

    def test_wrapped_bullets_are_joined(self):
        text = "## Done\n- 2026-09-22: first half\n  second half.\n\n## Next\n- Rerun Phase 7\n  after the season.\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual(got["stands"], "first half second half.")
        self.assertEqual(got["next"], "Rerun Phase 7 after the season.")

    def test_struck_through_next_items_are_skipped(self):
        text = "## Next\n- ~~old thing~~ done 2026-10-01\n- real thing\n"
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(text)["next"], "real thing")

    def test_a_subheading_inside_next_keeps_the_section(self):
        text = "## Next\n### This week\n- real thing\n"
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(text)["next"], "real thing")

    def test_long_lines_are_clipped(self):
        got = cards.parse_status("## Next\n- " + "x" * 400 + "\n")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(got["next"]), cards.CLIP)
        self.assertTrue(got["next"].endswith("…"))

    def test_card_carries_the_receiver_and_whether_one_is_needed(self):

150	def about_hits(db, path, q):
151	    """Question words in what the file says it is about: its name plus a frontmatter title/description line.
152	    Memory names are topic slugs and their description is a one-line summary; articles carry a title."""
153	    about = os.path.basename(path)[:-3].replace("_", " ").replace("-", " ")
154	    row = db.execute("SELECT body FROM d WHERE path = ?", (path,)).fetchone()
155	    if row:
156	        head = row[0].split("\n")[:40]  # body starts with the name line, then the frontmatter
157	        if len(head) > 1 and head[1].strip() == "---":
158	            for line in head[2:]:
159	                if line.strip() == "---":
160	                    break
161	                if line.startswith(("title:", "description:")):
162	                    about += " " + line.split(":", 1)[1]
163	    return len(set(keywords(q)) & set(tokens(about)))
164

166	def newest_copy(db, path):
167	    """Mac and old Windows slugs can hold the same memory file; the most recently changed copy wins."""
168	    name = os.path.basename(path)
169	    rows = [(m, p) for p, m in db.execute("SELECT path, mtime FROM seen WHERE path LIKE ?", ("%/" + name,))
170	            if os.path.basename(p) == name and tier_a(p)]
171	    return max(rows)[1] if rows else path

177	    articles and vault notes can be older than the memory that corrected them; the guard stops an
178	    off-topic memory jumping."""
179	    cands = [newest_copy(db, p) if tier_a(p) else p for p in fts5_top(db, q, max(limit, 3) + 3)]
180	    cands = list(dict.fromkeys(cands))
181	    a = next((p for p in cands[:3] if tier_a(p)), None)
182	    if a and a != cands[0] and about_hits(db, a, q) >= about_hits(db, cands[0], q):
183	        cands.remove(a)
184	        cands.insert(0, a)
185	    return cands[:limit]
186	
187

189	    n = db.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM seen").fetchone()[0] or 1

"""Checks recall.py's ladder on a temp tree: keywords, BM25 rank, index refresh, paragraph pick, pointer gate.
Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_recall.py  (reads nothing outside the temp tree)
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import tempfile

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "recall", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "recall.py"))
r = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(r)


def write(root, rel, text):
    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    with open(p, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(text)
    return p


# Keywords: filler dropped, suffixes meet their stems.
assert r.keywords("Why did the scanned pages fail, and how was it fixed?") == ["scan", "page", "fail", "fix"]

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
    filler = "\n\n".join(f"Filler paragraph {i} about unrelated weather and lunch." for i in range(120))
    write(root, "mem/project_push.md",
          "---\ndescription: \"cloud push note\"\n---\n\nIntro line.\n\n"
          "**Cause.** launchd cannot open Drive files that Terminal made.\n\n"
          + filler + "\n\n**Fix.** run the push inside Terminal.\n")
    write(root, "mem/project_decoy.md", "Drive backup timing and schedule.\n")
    db = r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "mem")], ":memory:")

    # Ranking: BM25 puts the file about the question ahead of the decoy.
    top = r.fts5_top(db, "why does the launchd push to Drive fail", 2)
    assert top[0].endswith("project_push.md"), top

    # Index refresh: a changed file is re-read, a deleted one drops out.
    disk = os.path.join(root, "disk.sqlite")
    r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "mem")], disk).close()
    os.remove(os.path.join(root, "mem/project_decoy.md"))
    db2 = r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "mem")], disk)
    assert not any(p.endswith("project_decoy.md") for p in r.fts5_top(db2, "backup schedule", 5))

    # Big file: only matching paragraphs come back, in document order, Cause before Fix.
    kws = r.keywords("launchd Drive cause and Terminal fix")
    chosen = r.best_paragraphs(os.path.join(root, "mem/project_push.md"), kws, r.idf_of(db, kws))
    texts = [c[4] for c in chosen]
    assert any("Cause" in t for t in texts) and any("Fix" in t for t in texts), texts
    assert texts.index(next(t for t in texts if "Cause" in t)) < texts.index(next(t for t in texts if "Fix" in t))
    assert not any("Filler" in t for t in texts)

    # Small file: returned whole.
    small = write(root, "mem/project_small.md", "One.\n\nTwo about tesseract.\n\nThree.\n")
    assert len(r.best_paragraphs(small, ["tesseract"], {})) == 3

    # Pointer gate: the target sits outside the index, so only the hop can reach it.
    target = write(root, "elsewhere/project_target.md", "Tesseract confuses the numbers five and nine.\n")
    write(root, "idx/project_src.md", f"Tesseract digits see `{target}`.\n")
    sdb = r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "idx")], ":memory:")
    _, _, ev = r.gather("tesseract digits", sdb)
    assert len(ev) == 1, ev  # closed: the file already covers the keywords
    _, _, ev = r.gather("tesseract confuses which numbers five nine", sdb)
    assert len(ev) == 2 and ev[1][0] == target, ev  # open: one hop

    # Tier A first: a memory file at #2 or #3 jumps a compiled article; the MEMORY.md index never does.
    kdir = os.path.join(root, "knowledge")
    mdir = os.path.join(root, ".claude/projects/-x/memory")
    write(kdir, "push-fix.md", "Drive push fix: grant Full Disk Access. Drive push fix. Drive push fix.\n")
    write(mdir, "project_push-fix.md", "Drive push fix: run it from Terminal.\n")
    write(mdir, "MEMORY.md", "- Drive push fix Drive push fix Drive push fix Drive push fix\n")
    tdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], ":memory:")
    assert not r.fts5_top(tdb, "drive push fix", 3)[0].endswith("project_push-fix.md")  # BM25 alone loses
    assert r.rank(tdb, "drive push fix", 3)[0].endswith("project_push-fix.md")
    assert r.rank(tdb, "drive push fix", 1) == [r.rank(tdb, "drive push fix", 3)[0]]
    # Name guard: a memory about something else stays below the article named for the question.
    write(kdir, "sleep-scheduler-project.md", "Sleep scheduler project. Sleep scheduler project.\n")
    write(mdir, "project_backup-sleepkill.md", "Backup task: sleep kill signature, scheduler project.\n")
    gdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], ":memory:")
    assert r.rank(gdb, "sleep scheduler project", 3)[0].endswith("sleep-scheduler-project.md")

    # Two machine slugs, same memory: only the newer copy is listed.
    wdir = os.path.join(root, ".claude/projects/-win/memory")
    newer = write(wdir, "project_push-fix.md", "Drive push fix: run it from Terminal (newer).\n")
    os.utime(newer, (2e9, 2e9))
    cdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir, wdir], ":memory:")
    got = r.rank(cdb, "drive push fix", 3)
    assert got[0] == newer and sum(p.endswith("project_push-fix.md") for p in got) == 1, got

    # Refresh writes each file once, even when it re-reads it.
    os.utime(os.path.join(kdir, "push-fix.md"))
    r.open_index([kdir, mdir], disk).close()
    ddb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], disk)
    assert ddb.execute("SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT path) FROM d").fetchone()[0] == 0

print("test_recall: all checks passed")

#!/bin/bash
# Recall bench: same questions, same model, two arms.
#   A = fresh default session in ~/DEV (finds the answer however it likes)
#   C = recall.py evidence (plain code) -> one model call, no tools
# Usage: bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh [A] [C]   (default: C only; ASET=held limits A to one set)
# Writes out/<arm><n>.json + .wall; score with: python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/score.py
# --no-session-persistence runs have no transcript. CLAUDE_INVOKED_BY makes the end-of-session hooks
# (transcript-capture, session-end, autopush, memsearch-sync) skip them; SessionStart still runs.
# Without it each run logged "transcript_path does not exist" to .errors.log (bursts on 2026-10-23).
export CLAUDE_INVOKED_BY=recall_bench
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"; OUT="$HERE/out"; mkdir -p "$OUT"
ARMS="${*:-C}"
now() { python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())'; }
cd ~/DEV || exit 1
n=0
grep -v '^#' "$HERE/questions.tsv" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r set q gtf gta; do
  n=$((n+1)); echo "== Q$n ($set)"
  if [[ " $ARMS " == *" A "* && ( -z "$ASET" || "$set" == "$ASET" ) ]]; then
    s=$(now)
    claude -p "$q Answer in 3 sentences or fewer." --model sonnet --output-format json \
      --permission-mode bypassPermissions --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 1 \
      < /dev/null > "$OUT/A$n.json" 2> "$OUT/A$n.err"
    echo "$s $(now)" > "$OUT/A$n.wall"
  fi
  if [[ " $ARMS " == *" C "* ]]; then
    s=$(now)
    python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "$q" > "$OUT/C$n.evidence" 2>&1
    m=$(now)
    claude -p "Answer the question using ONLY the evidence below, in 3 sentences or fewer. If the evidence does not answer it, say NOT FOUND.

Question: $q

Evidence:
$(cat "$OUT/C$n.evidence")" --model sonnet --output-format json --tools "" --strict-mcp-config \
      --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 1 < /dev/null > "$OUT/C$n.json" 2> "$OUT/C$n.err"
    echo "$s $m $(now)" > "$OUT/C$n.wall"
  fi
done
echo DONE
# set	question	ground-truth file	ground-truth answer

Anything rsyncing into the Google Drive for Desktop mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*/`) needs `--modify-window=5`. Diagnosed 2026-08-14 on `daily-backup.ps1` → `codex/sessions`: all 256 files size-identical, yet 134 re-sent nightly (252 MB). That is safe for append-only logs, where any real change also moves the size. Do not apply `--checksum` broadly — it re-reads every byte on both sides; it is cheap only bec

**How to apply:** when adding a new `Snapshot` call, ask whether the source can change without changing size. Databases, fixed-width records, and image/binary formats with in-place headers all can — give those `--checksum`. Logs and transcripts cannot — leave them on the window.

# Mac Sleep Freezes Long Drive-Reading Scripts

On 2026-10-06 a `landed.py` project-file scan showed no progress because it was frozen rather than slow: the Mac slept at 09:09, three minutes into the run, and the scan remained frozen on a Google Drive folder even after the machine woke. Re-running it with the Mac held awake via `caffeinate` completed in about four minutes. The fix generalizes an existing pattern — the backup skill had already b

## Key Points

- **A frozen run and a slow run look identical from the outside.** The question "how are you doing on this?" returned nothing not because the scan was mid-progress but because it had stopped; the absence of output was the whole signal available.
- **Waking the Mac does not resume the scan.** The freeze survived wake, so sleep during a Drive read is not a pause but a permanent stall requiring a re-run — meaning there is no "wait longer" recovery.
- **The true runtime was about four minutes.** Under `caffeinate` the same scan finished quickly, which retroactively proves the original hang was environmental rather than a performance problem in the script.
- **Sleep prevention belongs on the script, not on the operator.** The durable remedy is wrapping long Drive-reading work in `caffeinate` — the same change already applied to the backup skill — rather than remembering to keep the machine awake.
- **The scan's scope was also wrong:** `landed.py` reads `05_SYSTEMS/AI_Sessions_Backup`, a large session-backup folder that likely should be excluded, so part of the duration was work it should not have been doing.

## Details

The diagnostic shape here is worth separating from the fix. A long-running job that emits nothing is ambiguous between "working" and "dead", and the ambiguity is resolved only by changing a condition and re-running — here, holding the machine awake. That the second run took four minutes is what converts the first run's silence from "this is an expensive scan" into "this stalled at minute three", b

The two remedies operate at different layers and both are needed. Sleep prevention addresses the environment the script runs in, and placing it inside the script rather than in the operator's habits is what makes it durable — the backup skill had already taken this form, so the correction is really the recognition that `landed.py` belongs to the same class of work and should have inherited the sam

- [[concepts/in-session-background-process-limits]] — The adjacent constraint on long in-session work; sleep is a second way the execution context silently terminates a run.
- [[connections/the-execution-context-silently-edits-the-work-set]] — A host-state change shrinking or stopping what a run attempts without producing an error.
- [[connections/a-killed-process-leaves-debris-that-blocks-the-retry]] — The same non-self-healing pattern: an interrupted operation that stays quietly stuck rather than failing loudly.
- [[concepts/mac-owned-data-pulls-sleep-lateness]] — The prior instance of Mac sleep breaking scheduled data pulls, and the `pmset` wake option considered there.
- [[concepts/agent-file-status-and-path-reporting]] — The status-legibility gap behind "how are you doing on this?" returning nothing useful.
- [[concepts/silent-scheduled-task-failure-instrumentation]] — The companion case where the answer was instrumentation rather than a workaround.
- [[concepts/dev-folder-is-not-a-document-store]] — The same question of what belongs inside a scan's or manifest's scope.
- [[concepts/mac-stack-cleanup-closeout-2026-10-06]] — The closeout session that surfaced this and deferred both fixes.

# Mac Sleep Freezes Long Drive-Reading Scripts

On 2026-10-06 a `landed.py` project-file scan showed no progress because it was frozen rather than slow: the Mac slept at 09:09, three minutes into the run, and the scan remained frozen on a Google Drive folder even after the machine woke. Re-running it with the Mac held awake via `caffeinate` completed in about four minutes. The fix generalizes an existing pattern — the backup skill had already b

## Key Points

- **A frozen run and a slow run look identical from the outside.** The question "how are you doing on this?" returned nothing not because the scan was mid-progress but because it had stopped; the absence of output was the whole signal available.
- **Waking the Mac does not resume the scan.** The freeze survived wake, so sleep during a Drive read is not a pause but a permanent stall requiring a re-run — meaning there is no "wait longer" recovery.
- **The true runtime was about four minutes.** Under `caffeinate` the same scan finished quickly, which retroactively proves the original hang was environmental rather than a performance problem in the script.
- **Sleep prevention belongs on the script, not on the operator.** The durable remedy is wrapping long Drive-reading work in `caffeinate` — the same change already applied to the backup skill — rather than remembering to keep the machine awake.
- **The scan's scope was also wrong:** `landed.py` reads `05_SYSTEMS/AI_Sessions_Backup`, a large session-backup folder that likely should be excluded, so part of the duration was work it should not have been doing.

## Details

The diagnostic shape here is worth separating from the fix. A long-running job that emits nothing is ambiguous between "working" and "dead", and the ambiguity is resolved only by changing a condition and re-running — here, holding the machine awake. That the second run took four minutes is what converts the first run's silence from "this is an expensive scan" into "this stalled at minute three", b

The two remedies operate at different layers and both are needed. Sleep prevention addresses the environment the script runs in, and placing it inside the script rather than in the operator's habits is what makes it durable — the backup skill had already taken this form, so the correction is really the recognition that `landed.py` belongs to the same class of work and should have inherited the sam

Anything rsyncing into the Google Drive for Desktop mount (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*/`) needs `--modify-window=5`. Drive stores an mtime 1–2s below what rsync set, and for large files it stamps its own upload time instead (skew of hours). rsync's quick-check is size+mtime, so byte-identical files read as changed and are re-sent on **every** run, permanently.

Diagnosed 2026-08-14 on `daily-backup.ps1` → `codex/sessions`: all 256 files size-identical, yet 134 re-sent nightly (252 MB). That perpetual write load into FUSE is what fed the wedge the watchdog was catching — the snapshot had been failing since 2026-08-06 (rsync exit 23, then 1, then 124 once the watchdog landed).

**Why:** `du` on the mount reports less than the source (171M vs 289M) because Drive doesn't materialize every file — that discrepancy looks like an incomplete mirror and sends you hunting for missing data that isn't missing. Compare `stat -f%z` per file, not `du`.

**How to apply:**
- Diagnose with dry runs, not `du`: `rsync -an -i <src>/ <dst>/ | grep -c '^>f'` with and without `--modify-window=5`. A large gap between the two *is* the diagnosis.
- Files already stamped with Drive's own upload time need a one-time `touch -r <src> <dst>`; the flag alone won't close a multi-hour skew. The repair sticks across Drive re-sync.
- Never substitute `--size-only` — `claude-projects` has genuine same-size edits that only mtime catches.
- Genuinely-new files re-send under both settings (gemini's 428 were all NEW). If the count is identical with and without the window, it's real work, not this bug.

**`--modify-window` has a blind spot — cover it for SQLite (found 2026-08-15 while reviewing the fix).** The window makes rsync's quick-check tolerate a 5s mtime difference. That is safe for append-only logs, where any real change also moves the size. It is NOT safe for files rewritten in place at identical size — SQLite updates rows inside existing pages, so `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` (229,37

Fix in `daily-backup.ps1`: `Invoke-Rsync`/`Snapshot` take an `$extraArgs` param and the `.codex/sqlite` snapshot alone passes `--checksum`. Do not apply `--checksum` broadly — it re-reads every byte on both sides; it is cheap only bec

**How to apply:** when adding a new `Snapshot` call, ask whether the source can change without changing size. Databases, fixed-width records, and image/binary formats with in-place headers all can — give those `--checksum`. Logs and transcripts cannot — leave them on the window.
