"""Checks recall.py's ladder on a temp tree: keywords, BM25 rank, index refresh, paragraph pick, pointer gate.
Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/test_recall.py  (reads nothing outside the temp tree)
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import tempfile

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "recall", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "recall.py"))
r = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(r)


def write(root, rel, text):
    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    with open(p, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(text)
    return p


# Keywords: filler dropped, suffixes meet their stems.
assert r.keywords("Why did the scanned pages fail, and how was it fixed?") == ["scan", "page", "fail", "fix"]

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
    filler = "\n\n".join(f"Filler paragraph {i} about unrelated weather and lunch." for i in range(120))
    write(root, "mem/project_push.md",
          "---\ndescription: \"cloud push note\"\n---\n\nIntro line.\n\n"
          "**Cause.** launchd cannot open Drive files that Terminal made.\n\n"
          + filler + "\n\n**Fix.** run the push inside Terminal.\n")
    write(root, "mem/project_decoy.md", "Drive backup timing and schedule.\n")
    db = r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "mem")], ":memory:")

    # Ranking: BM25 puts the file about the question ahead of the decoy.
    top = r.fts5_top(db, "why does the launchd push to Drive fail", 2)
    assert top[0].endswith("project_push.md"), top

    # Index refresh: a changed file is re-read, a deleted one drops out.
    disk = os.path.join(root, "disk.sqlite")
    r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "mem")], disk).close()
    os.remove(os.path.join(root, "mem/project_decoy.md"))
    db2 = r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "mem")], disk)
    assert not any(p.endswith("project_decoy.md") for p in r.fts5_top(db2, "backup schedule", 5))

    # Big file: only matching paragraphs come back, in document order, Cause before Fix.
    kws = r.keywords("launchd Drive cause and Terminal fix")
    chosen = r.best_paragraphs(os.path.join(root, "mem/project_push.md"), kws, r.idf_of(db, kws))
    texts = [c[4] for c in chosen]
    assert any("Cause" in t for t in texts) and any("Fix" in t for t in texts), texts
    assert texts.index(next(t for t in texts if "Cause" in t)) < texts.index(next(t for t in texts if "Fix" in t))
    assert not any("Filler" in t for t in texts)

    # Small file: returned whole.
    small = write(root, "mem/project_small.md", "One.\n\nTwo about tesseract.\n\nThree.\n")
    assert len(r.best_paragraphs(small, ["tesseract"], {})) == 3

    # Pointer gate: the target sits outside the index, so only the hop can reach it.
    target = write(root, "elsewhere/project_target.md", "Tesseract confuses the numbers five and nine.\n")
    write(root, "idx/project_src.md", f"Tesseract digits see `{target}`.\n")
    sdb = r.open_index([os.path.join(root, "idx")], ":memory:")
    _, _, ev = r.gather("tesseract digits", sdb)
    assert len(ev) == 1, ev  # closed: the file already covers the keywords
    _, _, ev = r.gather("tesseract confuses which numbers five nine", sdb)
    assert len(ev) == 2 and ev[1][0] == target, ev  # open: one hop

    # Tier A first: a memory file at #2 or #3 jumps a compiled article; the MEMORY.md index never does.
    kdir = os.path.join(root, "knowledge")
    mdir = os.path.join(root, ".claude/projects/-x/memory")
    write(kdir, "push-fix.md", "Drive push fix: grant Full Disk Access. Drive push fix. Drive push fix.\n")
    write(mdir, "project_push-fix.md", "Drive push fix: run it from Terminal.\n")
    write(mdir, "MEMORY.md", "- Drive push fix Drive push fix Drive push fix Drive push fix\n")
    tdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], ":memory:")
    assert not r.fts5_top(tdb, "drive push fix", 3)[0].endswith("project_push-fix.md")  # BM25 alone loses
    assert r.rank(tdb, "drive push fix", 3)[0].endswith("project_push-fix.md")
    assert r.rank(tdb, "drive push fix", 1) == [r.rank(tdb, "drive push fix", 3)[0]]
    # Name guard: a memory about something else stays below the article named for the question.
    write(kdir, "sleep-scheduler-project.md", "Sleep scheduler project. Sleep scheduler project.\n")
    write(mdir, "project_backup-sleepkill.md", "Backup task: sleep kill signature, scheduler project.\n")
    gdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], ":memory:")
    assert r.rank(gdb, "sleep scheduler project", 3)[0].endswith("sleep-scheduler-project.md")

    # Two machine slugs, same memory: only the newer copy is listed.
    wdir = os.path.join(root, ".claude/projects/-win/memory")
    newer = write(wdir, "project_push-fix.md", "Drive push fix: run it from Terminal (newer).\n")
    os.utime(newer, (2e9, 2e9))
    cdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir, wdir], ":memory:")
    got = r.rank(cdb, "drive push fix", 3)
    assert got[0] == newer and sum(p.endswith("project_push-fix.md") for p in got) == 1, got

    # A memory whose name misses but whose description fits still jumps (bench Q3).
    write(kdir, "drive-hash-dedupe.md", "Copy file Drive mount folder skip. " * 3 + "\n")
    write(mdir, "project_fuse-hang.md",
          '---\ndescription: "Drive mount reads hang; copy a file with the API; every walk skips one folder"\n---\n'
          "Copy file Drive mount folder skip.\n")
    qdb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], ":memory:")
    q3 = "how to copy a file off the Drive mount and which folder to skip"
    assert not r.fts5_top(qdb, q3, 3)[0].endswith("project_fuse-hang.md")
    assert r.rank(qdb, q3, 3)[0].endswith("project_fuse-hang.md")

    # Refresh writes each file once, even when it re-reads it.
    os.utime(os.path.join(kdir, "push-fix.md"))
    r.open_index([kdir, mdir], disk).close()
    ddb = r.open_index([kdir, mdir], disk)
    assert ddb.execute("SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT path) FROM d").fetchone()[0] == 0

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- **Deliverables.** A finished file made for someone else this session (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a copy at `~/DEV/_DRIVE/03_REPORTS/YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>`. The repo keeps the source; Drive keeps the handed-off copy. Name the copy in the report.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If not empty, surface it and fix the hook issue if obvious, then append its lines to `transcripts/.errors.log.archived-<YYYY-MM-DD>` and clear it with `cp /dev/null` (same archive-then-clear step as backup and claude-stack-doctor; `: > file` is dcg-blocked).
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

content.text:
No. A hook would not help much here.

**Why not:**
- A hook runs on a fixed event, such as each message or each tool call. It cannot tell when an answer is wrong. Only you can see that.
- A hook that watches your words for "that's wrong" would fire often for no reason. Each time, it would add text to the session and cost tokens.
- `recall.py` already runs first without a hook. The fresh session test showed that.

**What would help instead (pick one):**
1. **Make the habit work in any session (I'd go with this one).** I change one line in your memory list, so that "add that to the recall test" leads any new session to the test-bench note. It takes about 1 minute and costs nothing to run.
2. **Run the test on a timer each month.** This is a scheduled job, not a hook. It costs about $0.60 a month. Its weak point is that the results land in a file that no one reads unless something alerts you.

Tell me if you want #1.

name: working-conditions-bottleneck
description: "Eric's self-identified bottleneck is working conditions, not effort — he needs a thinking partner / sharing outlet, and lacking one he goes looking for people and loses time"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: user
  originSessionId: 583baf57-8dc4-46c7-8842-501ae1fdeb04
  modified: 2026-08-03T23:18:09.932Z
---

Eric's limiting factor on deep work is environmental, not motivational. He is highly productive in short bursts once work actually starts; what breaks is the path to starting. The specific disruptor he named (2026-07-28) is the pull to share what he's working on — with no standing outlet for it, he goes and finds people, which costs him the session.

**Corrected 2026-07-29.** The pull toward people is not a leak, it's the generative stage. His own observation: alone he wants company; in company the project ideas arrive. Solitude is where he refines, not where he generates. A long unbroken solo block with nothing in the hopper is waiting, not deep work.

**Second brake, same day:** he holds ideas back from fear of overstepping into others' lanes, against an unstated expectation that he act unasked. He is deliberately moving off this position ("if I don't act, ideas wither"). Pressfield's Resistance is his frame for it.

**Qualified 2026-08-03.** The permission gate is not entirely self-imposed. He acted unasked on a device another staffer was already championing (ShiftWave chair, second trial unit) and took real organizational blowback for it — careful, low-key handling bought nothing, because the claim was made by initiating, not by presenting. So the caution is warranted on ground someone has visibly attached themselves to, and unwarranted everywhere else. His same-day reaction ("pander to the people in power, keep your head down") is a bruise, not necessarily a settled position — don't treat it as one.

**Why:** Both reframe what looks like procrastination. The first is an unmet structural need (input/ideation) improvising in real time; the second is a self-imposed permission gate that reads as professional courtesy. Neither is a discipline failure, and treating them as one produces useless advice.

**How to apply:** Act as the thinking partner in-session — reflect his reasoning back, name what's interesting in it, and give him something to react to rather than only executing tasks silently. When he's ideating, don't rush to implementation; the ideation *is* the need being met, and it's the stage that feeds everything else — help him capture what surfaces. Prefer short, well-scoped blocks with a clear starting line. When he hesitates on whether something is his to do, first ask whether anyone has visibly claimed it — if not, name the permission gate rather than validating the caution; if someone has, the hesitation is a correct read and the useful move is how to approach the owner, not encouragement to proceed. Related: [[company-generates-solitude-refines]], [[waiting-for-the-ask-kills-the-idea]], [[ownership-not-merit-governs-the-reaction]], [[design-the-conditions-not-the-discipline]] in the SecondBrain vault.

**Second brake, same day:** he holds ideas back from fear of overstepping into others' lanes, against an unstated expectation that he act unasked. He is deliberately moving off this position ("if I don't act, ideas wither"). Pressfield's Resistance is his frame for it.

He acted unasked on a device another staffer was already championing (ShiftWave chair, second trial unit) and took real organizational blowback for it — careful, low-key handling bought nothing, because the claim was made by initiating, not by presenting. # Unattended follow-up to a scheduled reindex + recall eval (Task Scheduler, \Eric\memsearch-drain-*).
# Runs as the last action of the task, after memsearch-drain.ps1 and recall-eval.py:
#   1. checks the index finished (memsearch-drain.log ends in exit=0),
#   2. checks recall-eval wrote ledger rows in the last 24 h,
#   3. commits + pushes the ledger and results in ~/.claude (nothing else on Windows does),
#   4. writes LATEST.md here with the rows,
#   5. ONLY on a problem, appends one line to .errors.log, which every session surfaces
#      at startup (same pattern as claude-stack-doctor/weekly-check.ps1).
param([string]$Label = '', [switch]$Test)   # -Test: no git, no .errors.log

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$claude = Join-Path $HOME '.claude'
$errLog = Join-Path $claude 'global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log'
$problems = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

$drainLog = Join-Path $claude 'scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
$drainLast = if (Test-Path $drainLog) { Get-Content $drainLog -Tail 1 } else { '' }
$indexOk = $drainLast -match 'exit=0'
if (-not $indexOk) { $problems.Add("index did not finish cleanly (last drain line: '$drainLast')") }

$ledger = Join-Path $here 'ledger.md'
$since = (Get-Date).AddHours(-24).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
$rows = @()
if (Test-Path $ledger) {
    $rows = @(Get-Content $ledger | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\| (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) ' -and $Matches[1] -ge $since -and (-not $Label -or $_ -match [regex]::Escape("| $Label"))})
}
if ($rows.Count -eq 0) {
    $last = Join-Path $here "logs\last-$Label.txt"   # written by run-eval.ps1
    $why = if (Test-Path $last) { " [$((Get-Content -LiteralPath $last -Raw).Trim())]" } else { '' }
    $problems.Add("recall-eval wrote no ledger rows$(if ($Label) { " labelled '$Label'" }) in the last 24 h$why")
}

$git = 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe'
$pushed = $false
if ($rows.Count -gt 0 -and -not $Test) {
    & $git -C $claude add -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
    & $git -C $claude diff --cached --quiet -- audits/recall-eval
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        & $git -C $claude commit -q -m "recall-eval: scheduled run $(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd) $Label" -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude pull -q --no-rebase --no-edit 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude push -q 2>&1 | Out-Null
        $pushed = $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0
        if (-not $pushed) { $problems.Add('commit made but git push failed (run git pull/push in ~/.claude)') }
    } else { $pushed = $true }
}

$status = if ($problems.Count) { 'PROBLEM: ' + ($problems -join '; ') } else { 'OK' }
@(
    "# Latest scheduled recall eval"
    ""
    "Run finished $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') on $env:COMPUTERNAME. Status: $status"
    "Index: $drainLast"
    ""
    "| date | machine | label | backend | n | hit@1 | hit@5 | MRR | p50 ms | p95 ms | fail% | coverage% | by layer (hit@5) |"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
) + $rows | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $here 'LATEST.md') -Encoding utf8

if ($problems.Count -and -not $Test) {
    Add-Content -LiteralPath $errLog -Encoding utf8 -Value "[$(Get-Date -Format o)] recall-eval scheduled run: $($problems -join '; ') - see ~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/LATEST.md"

# Unattended follow-up to a scheduled reindex + recall eval (Task Scheduler, \Eric\memsearch-drain-*).
# Runs as the last action of the task, after memsearch-drain.ps1 and recall-eval.py:
#   1. checks the index finished (memsearch-drain.log ends in exit=0),
#   2. checks recall-eval wrote ledger rows in the last 24 h,
#   3. commits + pushes the ledger and results in ~/.claude (nothing else on Windows does),
#   4. writes LATEST.md here with the rows,
#   5. ONLY on a problem, appends one line to .errors.log, which every session surfaces
#      at startup (same pattern as claude-stack-doctor/weekly-check.ps1).
param([string]$Label = '', [switch]$Test)   # -Test: no git, no .errors.log

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$claude = Join-Path $HOME '.claude'
$errLog = Join-Path $claude 'global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log'
$problems = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

$drainLog = Join-Path $claude 'scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
$drainLast = if (Test-Path $drainLog) { Get-Content $drainLog -Tail 1 } else { '' }
$indexOk = $drainLast -match 'exit=0'
if (-not $indexOk) { $problems.Add("index did not finish cleanly (last drain line: '$drainLast')") }

$ledger = Join-Path $here 'ledger.md'
$since = (Get-Date).AddHours(-24).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
$rows = @()
if (Test-Path $ledger) {
    $rows = @(Get-Content $ledger | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\| (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) ' -and $Matches[1] -ge $since -and (-not $Label -or $_ -match [regex]::Escape("| $Label"))})
}
if ($rows.Count -eq 0) {
    $last = Join-Path $here "logs\last-$Label.txt"   # written by run-eval.ps1
    $why = if (Test-Path $last) { " [$((Get-Content -LiteralPath $last -Raw).Trim())]" } else { '' }
    $problems.Add("recall-eval wrote no ledger rows$(if ($Label) { " labelled '$Label'" }) in the last 24 h$why")
}

$git = 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe'
$pushed = $false
if ($rows.Count -gt 0 -and -not $Test) {
    & $git -C $claude add -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
    & $git -C $claude diff --cached --quiet -- audits/recall-eval
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        & $git -C $claude commit -q -m "recall-eval: scheduled run $(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd) $Label" -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude pull -q --no-rebase --no-edit 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude push -q 2>&1 | Out-Null
        $pushed = $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0
        if (-not $pushed) { $problems.Add('commit made but git push failed (run git pull/push in ~/.claude)') }
    } else { $pushed = $true }
}

$status = if ($problems.Count) { 'PROBLEM: ' + ($problems -join '; ') } else { 'OK' }
@(
    "# Latest scheduled recall eval"
    ""
    "Run finished $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') on $env:COMPUTERNAME. Status: $status"
    "Index: $drainLast"
    ""
    "| date | machine | label | backend | n | hit@1 | hit@5 | MRR | p50 ms | p95 ms | fail% | coverage% | by layer (hit@5) |"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
) + $rows | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $here 'LATEST.md') -Encoding utf8

if ($problems.Count -and -not $Test) {
    Add-Content -LiteralPath $errLog -Encoding utf8 -Value "[$(Get-Date -Format o)] recall-eval scheduled run: $($problems -join '; ') - see ~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/LATEST.md"

"""Unattended recall check: does recall.py still open the right file? No model call, seconds.

Asks recall.py every question in the 30-case eval (audits/recall-eval/questions.jsonl) and the
bench (questions.tsv here), and compares with baseline.json. Prints one line. Exit 1 when a
score drops below the baseline, so the daily backup logs it to .errors.log, which every
session shows at startup. Nobody has to remember to run it.

Usage:
    python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/check.py                     # check
    python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/check.py --update-baseline   # after a deliberate change
"""
import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
HOME = os.path.expanduser("~")
EVAL = os.path.join(HOME, ".claude/audits/recall-eval/questions.jsonl")
BENCH = os.path.join(HERE, "questions.tsv")
BASELINE = os.path.join(HERE, "baseline.json")

_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("recall", os.path.join(HERE, "..", "recall.py"))
recall = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(recall)


def rank_of(files, expected):
    """1-based rank of the first file whose path contains an expected fragment (recall-eval's rule)."""
    for i, f in enumerate(files, 1):
        if any(e.lower() in f.replace("\\", "/").lower() for e in expected):
            return i
    return None


def scores(db):
    cases = [json.loads(l) for l in open(EVAL, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
    ranks = [rank_of(recall.rank(db, c["query"], 5), c["expected"]) for c in cases]
    rows = [l.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for l in open(BENCH, encoding="utf-8")
            if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
    top1 = sum(1 for r in rows if rank_of(recall.rank(db, r[1], 1), [os.path.basename(r[2])]) == 1)
    return {"eval_hit1": sum(r == 1 for r in ranks), "eval_hit5": sum(r is not None for r in ranks),
            "eval_n": len(cases), "bench_top1": top1, "bench_n": len(rows)}


def drops(now, base):
    """Scores below the baseline. A bigger question set with the same hits is not a drop."""
    return [f"{k} {now[k]} < {base[k]}" for k in ("eval_hit1", "eval_hit5", "bench_top1")
            if k in base and now[k] < base[k]]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--update-baseline", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    now = scores(recall.open_index(recall.roots()))
    line = (f"eval hit@1 {now['eval_hit1']}/{now['eval_n']} hit@5 {now['eval_hit5']}/{now['eval_n']}, "
            f"bench top-1 {now['bench_top1']}/{now['bench_n']}")
    if a.update_baseline:
        with open(BASELINE, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(now, fh, indent=2)
        print(f"recall-check: baseline set: {line}")
        return 0
    try:
        base = json.load(open(BASELINE, encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        print(f"recall-check: no baseline ({BASELINE}); run with --update-baseline. Now: {line}")
        return 1
    bad = drops(now, base)
    if bad:
        print(f"recall-check: DROP {'; '.join(bad)} ({line}). recall.py now opens a worse file for some "
              f"questions: compare with ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/results.md, or --update-baseline if intended")
        return 1
    print(f"recall-check: OK {line}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Unattended recall check: does recall.py still open the right file? No model call, seconds.

Asks recall.py every question in the 30-case eval (audits/recall-eval/questions.jsonl) and the
bench (questions.tsv here), and compares with baseline.json. Prints one line. Exit 1 when a
score drops below the baseline, so the daily backup logs it to .errors.log, which every
session shows at startup. Nobody has to remember to run it.

Usage:
    python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/check.py                     # check
    python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/check.py --update-baseline   # after a deliberate change
"""
import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
HOME = os.path.expanduser("~")
EVAL = os.path.join(HOME, ".claude/audits/recall-eval/questions.jsonl")
BENCH = os.path.join(HERE, "questions.tsv")
BASELINE = os.path.join(HERE, "baseline.json")

_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("recall", os.path.join(HERE, "..", "recall.py"))
recall = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(recall)


def rank_of(files, expected):
    """1-based rank of the first file whose path contains an expected fragment (recall-eval's rule)."""
    for i, f in enumerate(files, 1):
        if any(e.lower() in f.replace("\\", "/").lower() for e in expected):
            return i
    return None


def scores(db):
    cases = [json.loads(l) for l in open(EVAL, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
    ranks = [rank_of(recall.rank(db, c["query"], 5), c["expected"]) for c in cases]
    rows = [l.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for l in open(BENCH, encoding="utf-8")
            if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
    top1 = sum(1 for r in rows if rank_of(recall.rank(db, r[1], 1), [os.path.basename(r[2])]) == 1)
    return {"eval_hit1": sum(r == 1 for r in ranks), "eval_hit5": sum(r is not None for r in ranks),
            "eval_n": len(cases), "bench_top1": top1, "bench_n": len(rows)}


def drops(now, base):
    """Scores below the baseline. A bigger question set with the same hits is not a drop."""
    return [f"{k} {now[k]} < {base[k]}" for k in ("eval_hit1", "eval_hit5", "bench_top1")
            if k in base and now[k] < base[k]]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--update-baseline", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    now = scores(recall.open_index(recall.roots()))
    line = (f"eval hit@1 {now['eval_hit1']}/{now['eval_n']} hit@5 {now['eval_hit5']}/{now['eval_n']}, "
            f"bench top-1 {now['bench_top1']}/{now['bench_n']}")
    if a.update_baseline:
        with open(BASELINE, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(now, fh, indent=2)
        print(f"recall-check: baseline set: {line}")
        return 0
    try:
        base = json.load(open(BASELINE, encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        print(f"recall-check: no baseline ({BASELINE}); run with --update-baseline. Now: {line}")
        return 1
    bad = drops(now, base)
    if bad:
        print(f"recall-check: DROP {'; '.join(bad)} ({line}). recall.py now opens a worse file for some "
              f"questions: compare with ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/results.md, or --update-baseline if intended")
        return 1
    print(f"recall-check: OK {line}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: memory-write
description: >-
  Writes, updates, removes, and recalls facts in the two-tier memory system
  (~/.claude/global-memory/ and ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/). Use for write
  requests such as "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", and
  "forget about", and for recall requests such as "did we already…?", "what did we
  decide about X?", and "do you remember…?". Picks the tier, dedups, and enforces caps;
  recall checks the injected snapshot, then recall.py, then memsearch. Do not use for a story or lesson
  worth a vault note (use capture-insight) or an article to keep (use ingest-resource).
---

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below. Do it in one call, from the project folder (the slug comes from the current folder; `--dir` overrides):
     `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <bare-slug> --desc "<one line>" --hook "<when to open>" [--why "..." --how "..."] "<fact>"`
     It checks the name rule, refuses an existing or look-alike name (exit 2: read that file, then `--update` it or `--force`), writes the file and the index line, runs steps 1 and 4 of the Verification Gate, and refreshes recall.py's index. `PASS` covers those checks; step 3 (contradictions) is still yours.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: BM25 keyword rank over the memsearch paths plus the whole vault, a Tier A memory first, then it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs with line numbers. Answer from that. If the printed paragraphs miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the words in the question are not the words in the notes: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-` (Mac `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`; the Mac keeps `_`: `~/DEV/CLI_Dev` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-CLI_Dev`; Windows `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV`; `00_Primary_Storage_Drive` → `00-Primary-Storage-Drive`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

# Machine

Machine-specific shell, paths, and traps live in `~/.claude/machine.md`. Read that file first. On a new machine copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md`.

The Mac (`~/DEV`) runs everything. The Baylor Windows laptop (`~/Desktop/DEV`) is used only for desktop-app sessions since 2026-10-21, with no automation. Projects sync through GitHub (`erash11`), documents through Google Drive.

**Session routine.** When working inside a project repo, follow the Session routine in its `AGENTS.md`: `git pull` and read `docs/STATUS.md` at the start; update `STATUS.md`, commit, and `git push` at the end.

# Workflow Expectations

- One home: the "Workflow Expectations" section of `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read it there.

# graphify

- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) — turns any input into a knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`. When the user types `/graphify`, run that skill's workflow before doing anything else.

---

> **Why this file is not identical to `CLAUDE.md`.** Claude Code has a Skill tool, so `CLAUDE.md` routes memory work to the `memory-write` skill instead of restating it. Harnesses reading this file have no such tool, so the memory rules are spelled out below in full. The divergence is deliberate. **Do not symlink these two files together.** The canonical, most detailed copy is `~/.claude/skills/memory-write/SKILL.md` — if a rule below ever disagrees with that file, that file wins.

# Memory System

Two tiers.

## Tier A — per-project structured facts
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` — one file per durable fact, indexed by `MEMORY.md`. The active project's Tier A memory is **auto-injected each session**. Write here for stable facts: user profile entries, project conventions, feedback rules. Also indexed by memsearch, so recallable cross-project.

File naming by type: `user_*.md`, `project_*.md`, `feedback_*.md`, `reference_*.md`. Each needs frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) plus a one-line pointer added to that slug's `MEMORY.md`. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <slug> --desc "..." --hook "..." [--why ... --how ...] "fact"` does both, refuses duplicates (`--update` replaces), and runs the read-back check; run it from the project folder so the slug is right.

**Slugs.** The slug is the absolute cwd with every character other than a letter or digit replaced by `-`:
- Mac: `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`
- Windows: `~/Desktop/DEV` → `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV` · `~/.claude/skills` → `C--Users-eric-rash--claude-skills`

**Slugs differ per machine.** The same project is `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-<X>` on the Mac and `C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-<X>` on Windows. Tier A written on one machine is not auto-injected on the other; memsearch still finds it. Prefer writing durable project facts to the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.

## Tier B — global working memory
`~/.claude/global-memory/`, loaded every session regardless of cwd:
- `USER.md` — durable user profile. **1,375 character cap.**
- `MEMORY.md` — active threads, environment notes, pending decisions. **2,500 character cap.**
- `transcripts/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — auto-captured turn summaries (Stop hook).

Check `wc -c` before writing. If over cap, consolidate existing entries before adding.

## Daily compiled logs (separate system, read-only)
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, produced by `claude-memory-compiler` via its own hooks. Only the compiler writes them. Read one only when a question needs that day; the injected snapshot is the source of truth.

## Session startup (read without comment)

> Kept as a manual instruction on purpose. Claude Code does this with the
> `keystone-unified-snapshot.js` SessionStart hook, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer
> states it. Codex has no equivalent hook, so the steps stay spelled out here.
> Do not "align" the two files by deleting this section.
Read in this order: `global-memory/USER.md`, then `global-memory/MEMORY.md`, then `global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. The one thing to say out loud: if `.errors.log` is non-empty, give a one-line-per-kind summary (kind, count, latest message) on the first response, then continue. Entries mean a hook or scheduled job failed.

These are a **frozen snapshot** — loaded once. Mid-session writes persist to disk but take effect next session. This preserves the prefix cache. Load anything further only when a question needs it.

## Writing — the steps
On "remember this", "note that", "update memory", "save this", "forget about":
1. Decide tier — "will this be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. No / only matters now → Tier B.
2. Read the target file in full.
3. Dedup check (substring scan).
4. Cap check (`wc -c`) for Tier B.
5. If over cap, consolidate before adding.
6. Write.
7. Confirm in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

For **remove**: confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder
Climb in order; stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run a search when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs. If they miss the answer, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2** — on `NO MATCH`, or when the question's words are not the notes' words: `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword, ~1 min.
4. **L3** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
5. **L4** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback** — "I don't have a record of that."

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/backup

# Backup

Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` right now. Same script the `com.keystone.dailybackup`
launchd agent runs at 21:00 daily (moved from 09:00 on 2026-09-24, when the Mac became the evening machine) — this is the on-demand path for when the Mac was shut at 21:00.

## Run it

Do not pre-check anything. Run first, report after.

```bash
/usr/bin/caffeinate -i /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
```

Use a Bash `timeout` of `600000` (10 min). An awake run takes ~5-10 min, most of it the memsearch
INDEX step. Keep `caffeinate -i`: without it the Mac idle-sleeps on battery the moment the copies
finish, and INDEX crawls through brief dark wakes. On 2026-10-06 that turned a ~6 min index into
2 h. If a run outlasts the timeout, it moves to the background; wait for it, do not re-run.

## Read the verdict from state, not from the tail

```bash
cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json
```

`status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. That file is the authority.
The tail is for diagnosing, not for deciding.

**`status: OK` is not "everything was saved" — read `okCount` too.** A run that skipped the
SSD still ends `OK` with 0 errors. See the SSD gotcha below for what the count means.

## Then clear the stale hook error, if any

A failed run appends a line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`, which is surfaced
as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. A later successful run does **not** clear it. If `status`
is now `OK` and the file contains only `daily-backup:` lines, archive and empty it:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

If any non-`daily-backup` line is present, leave the file alone and tell the user what else is in it.
Shell truncation (`: > file`) under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule
`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`, and there is no `truncate` binary here — use `cp /dev/null`.

## Report

Three lines, plain: did it work, what was skipped, what to do next. Never report "backup complete"
without naming a skipped target — a silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to prevent.

## Gotchas

**Safe to ignore — expected on a healthy run:**
- `SNAP skip (missing): ~/.codex/memories` — that path has never existed.
